evals.name: check-never-runs
evals.prompt: Our flake uses blueprint and nix/formatter.nix builds a treefmt wrapper ending with: formatter // { meta = formatter.meta // { tests = { check = check; }; }; }. CI runs nix flake check and stays green even when I commit deliberately misformatted Nix code. Why, and how do I fix it?
evals.trap: The green CI tempts blaming treefmt config or cache; the real bug is meta.tests — the check derivation is never collected into checks

assertions.text: Identifies that tests must live under passthru.tests, not meta.tests
Rewrites the tail as formatter // { passthru = formatter.passthru // { tests.check = check; }; }
Verifies pkgs-formatter-check appears via nix eval .#checks.<sys> --apply builtins.attrNames
Does not blame treefmt cache or suggest deleting .direnv/store paths

evals.name: add-python-formatting
evals.prompt: Add Python formatting and linting to this repo's existing nix/formatter.nix (it already handles nix and shell via treefmt-nix mkWrapper). We use ruff.
evals.trap: Tempts enabling ruff-format only, enabling both without priorities so order falls to name order, or cargo-culting the nonexistent pipeline option

assertions.text: Enables both ruff-check and ruff-format in programs
Orders them with priority: ruff-check priority 1, ruff-format priority 2 (and does not use the nonexistent pipeline option)
Edits formatter.nix only — no new flake outputs, no pre-commit hooks invented

evals.name: vendored-tree-conflicts
evals.prompt: nix fmt keeps reformatting files under .agents/skills/ and .specify/ (vendored from upstream repos), so every upstream refresh produces a huge diff and shellcheck errors on scripts we don't own. Stop treefmt from touching them.
evals.trap: Tempts per-formatter excludes repeated N times or .gitignore hacks; the tool for this is settings.global.excludes

assertions.text: Adds settings.excludes (or the pre-rename settings.global.excludes) with the vendored globs (e.g. ".agents/**", ".specify/**")
Does not suggest gitignoring tracked vendored files or disabling shellcheck globally

evals.name: envrc-not-formatted
evals.prompt: shellcheck and shfmt run via treefmt in our flake, but .envrc and .envrc.local never get checked or formatted even though they are tracked bash files. Why?
evals.trap: Tempts blaming treefmt file detection or git; the cause is that shell formatters only match *.sh/*.bash by default and need explicit includes

assertions.text: Explains that .envrc doesn't match the default shell file patterns
Adds includes = [ "*.sh" "*.bash" "*.envrc" "*.envrc.*" ] to BOTH shellcheck and shfmt formatter settings

evals.name: write-format-check-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Our blueprint repo has nix/formatter.nix with a working treefmt-nix mkWrapper but no format enforcement in CI. Add a check so nix flake check fails when the tree is not formatted. CI is Linux-only; don't add a new workflow job.
evals.trap: Tempts adding a separate CI job running nix fmt + git diff, or a non-hermetic check reading the working tree; the pattern is treefmt-nix's build.check (or an equivalent hermetic runCommand) attached via passthru.tests

assertions.text: Uses evalModule's config.build.check flake (preferred) or an equivalent hermetic runCommand copying ${flake} and failing on git diff
Attaches it via passthru.tests.check on the formatter derivation (no new flake.nix outputs, no CI job)

evals.name: deadnix-eats-module-arg
evals.prompt: After running nix fmt, a NixOS module broke: the { flake, ... } argument we kept for future use was deleted from the lambda header by the formatter. What happened and how do we keep intentionally-unused args?
evals.trap: Tempts disabling deadnix entirely; the targeted fixes are programs.deadnix.no-lambda-pattern-names (for callPackage-style pattern sets) or the underscore-prefix convention

assertions.text: Identifies deadnix as the formatter that removes unused lambda args
Recommends programs.deadnix.no-lambda-pattern-names = true and/or underscore-prefixed names (_flake) rather than disabling deadnix

evals.name: default-excludes-surprise
evals.prompt: Our treefmt-nix setup enables taplo and mdformat, but treefmt never touches go.mod, flake.lock or LICENSE even though they're tracked, and I never excluded them. Also, some stray .conf files get no formatting and no warning at all. Explain both and make uncovered files visible.
evals.trap: Tempts blaming includes patterns or the git walker; the causes are enableDefaultExcludes (true by default, covers *.lock, go.mod, LICENSE...) and on-unmatched defaulting to silence

assertions.text: Attributes the skipped files to enableDefaultExcludes = true and lists that it covers lock files, go.mod/go.sum, LICENSE etc.
Sets settings.on-unmatched (e.g. "warn") to surface files no formatter covers
Only disables enableDefaultExcludes if those files should genuinely be formatted
